page: Google Cloud Platform m2-ultramem-416 is a memory-optimized cloud server engineered for massive scale-up enterprise workloads. The system is powered by Intel Xeon x86_64 processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. Compute resources comprise 416 dedicated virtual CPUs across 208 physical cores with two threads per core. Architectural instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography and BMI2 bit-manipulation extensions. The platform features an extensive cache hierarchy, offering 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 38 MB of shared L3 cache.

Memory capacity is the defining specification of the m2-ultramem-416, provisioning 11,776.0 GB (approximately 11.5 TB) of RAM, which equates to 28.31 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware benchmarks reveal exceptional multi-channel throughput, clocking 20,571.16 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 658.18 GB/sec for large-block uncached read operations, supplemented by 296.37 GB/sec write bandwidth. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero hardware accelerators or GPUs. Network allocation includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external configuration for remote connectivity.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the strengths and structural tradeoffs of a high-density, multi-socket architecture. Multi-threaded compute capacity is exceptionally strong, achieving 353,160.93 points on stress-ng and 101,658.81 on the PassMark CPU test suite, while PassMark extended instructions reached 331,945.98. In-memory operations excel, highlighted by Redis SET performance measuring 324.46 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 126.25 GB/sec. Conversely, per-core metrics show constraints typical of massive NUMA topologies, with single-core stress-ng (1,326.29) and single-core Geekbench (1,004.0) falling into lower benchmark percentiles. Sequential compression tasks also exhibit lower single-thread efficiency.

In qualitative terms, the server represents high operational cost efficiency for specific scale-up architectures that cannot be decomposed into distributed clusters. By consolidating petabyte-scale data pipelines or multi-terabyte in-memory tables onto a single operating system instance, it eliminates inter-node network serialization latencies. The instance profile is primarily aligned with SAP HANA, ultra-large enterprise in-memory relational databases, high-throughput Redis caching farms, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform m2-ultramem-416 is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 416 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs across 208 physical cores clocked at 2.7 GHz, delivering 11,776 GB of system RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, it features a massive memory density of 28.31 GB per vCPU and achieves uncached read bandwidth exceeding 658 GB/sec. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, focusing hardware resources entirely on core computing and memory capacity. Benchmark results indicate exceptional aggregate multi-core processing power and high-speed in-memory operations, demonstrated by top-tier Redis throughput and PassMark scores, despite moderate single-threaded execution speed. This server is engineered specifically for massive in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, large-scale caching tiers, and memory-bound transactional data processing.
